note: Verified SPDX licenses for the third-party tools this toolkit references, so
that license ACCURACY stays checked continuously (scripts/verify-licenses.mjs).
Every 'spdx' below was confirmed against the primary source — the upstream
repository's own LICENSE via the GitHub license API and/or the raw file — not
from memory. A tool with no GitHub repo (or whose license GitHub cannot detect)
carries a 'rawUrl' + 'needles' instead of relying on the API alone.
Audit of 2026-10-13 corrected five rows that had been wrong:
ghidriff  Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0   (raw LICENSE confirms GPLv3)
YARA-X    Apache-2.0 -> BSD-3-Clause
msynth    BSD-3      -> GPL-2.0   (raw LICENSE confirms GPLv2)
Diaphora  GPL-3.0    -> AGPL-3.0
AFL++     Apache-2.0 -> AGPL-3.0  (raw LICENSE confirms AGPLv3)
(DynamoRIO was filed as copyleft; it is BSD-3, permissive)
Audit of 2026-10-13 (round 2; GitHub license API + the raw LICENSE of each repo)
corrected EIGHT more rows that had been wrong, and added the Windows-relevant batch:
Keystone  BSD-3     -> GPL-2.0    (COPYING is GPLv2)
de4dot-cex MIT      -> GPL-3.0    (COPYING is GPLv3)
Speakeasy Apache-2.0 -> MIT       (LICENSE.txt is MIT)
TitanHide  GPL-3.0  -> MIT        (relicensed upstream)
al-khaser GPL-3.0   -> GPL-2.0    (LICENSE is GPLv2)
PE-bear   MIT       -> GPL-2.0    (LICENSE is GPLv2)
D-810     MIT       -> AGPL-3.0   (LICENSE is AGPLv3)
objection MIT       -> GPL-3.0    (LICENSE is GPLv3)
Same round: the runtimes and infra tools the bootstrap installs (Zig, CMake, Ninja,
Rust, Python, Node, radare2, retoolkit, Frida, Wireshark, QEMU, Fluxzy) were added
too, so the coverage number reports the real gap instead of an empty one. Tools with
no GitHub repo and no readable LICENSE (Procmon, API Monitor, WSL/Ubuntu, and the
firmware trio ubireader/sasquatch/firmware-mod-kit) are deliberately ABSENT: the
registry only holds lines that a primary source can actually confirm.
Rust  is dual MIT OR Apache-2.0; the API detects the Apache half, which is what
the row declares (LICENSE-APACHE is checked raw as well).
Frida is under the wxWindows Library Licence 3.1 (SPDX deprecates 'wxWindows' in
favour of LGPL-2.0+ with the WxWindows exception) — GitHub cannot detect it,
so the raw COPYING is the evidence.
Audit of 2026-10-13 (round 3) added SIX tools that the documentation already cites but
that had no verified line. Each was confirmed twice — the repo's own LICENSE raw file
(the 'needles' below) AND GitHub's own detection — and none was written from memory:
XED (intelxed/xed), WinAFL (googleprojectzero/winafl), System Informer
(winsiderss/systeminformer), Cutter (rizinorg/cutter), pefile (erocarrera/pefile),
FLOSS (mandiant/flare-floss).
Two labels are easy to get wrong and are therefore pinned by the raw file:
System Informer is MIT (LICENSE.txt), NOT the GPL people assume from its history as
Process Hacker; FLOSS is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE.txt).
Still deliberately ABSENT (no primary source can confirm a line): Procmon, API Monitor,
WSL/Ubuntu and the firmware trio ubireader/sasquatch/firmware-mod-kit. The registry holds
only what a primary source actually says.
